## Summary

UK public bodies spent £3.4 billion on private consultants in 2023-24, representing a £1.3 billion increase compared to 2019-20 figures. This surge in spending, which peaked during the Covid pandemic, has not returned to pre-pandemic levels.

The figures highlight a significant challenge for Prime Minister Keir Starmer's government, which has pledged to cut consultant spending in half during its current parliamentary term. Despite this goal, nearly £650 million in new government contracts have been awarded to consultants since Labour came to power, including a £223 million deal with KPMG to train civil servants over the next 15 months.

Labour peer and finance academic Prem Sikka strongly criticized the practice, calling it "scandalous" and arguing that a culture of over-reliance on consultants has taken hold. He questioned the value consultants provide, suggesting it is unrealistic for them to deliver meaningful insights after spending only a short time within complex organizations.
